125. OWASP Top 10

Security

OWASP Top 10 is a list of the most critical web application security risks published by OWASP. It helps developers identify, understand, and prevent the most common security vulnerabilities found in modern applications.

Common OWASP Risks

  • Broken Access Control
  • Cryptographic Failures
  • Injection Attacks
  • Insecure Design
  • Security Misconfiguration
  • Vulnerable Components
  • Authentication Failures

Real Project Example

Consider an API endpoint that allows access to user information without proper authorization checks.

Vulnerable Request
GET /api/users/1

If authorization is not enforced, any authenticated user could access another user's information. This is known as a Broken Access Control vulnerability.

Follow-up Questions

Q: Why should developers know OWASP?

OWASP covers the most common security vulnerabilities and provides guidance for preventing them during development.

Q: Which OWASP issue is most common?

Broken Access Control is consistently one of the most common and highest-impact security risks.

Senior-Level Follow-up

Q: How do OWASP guidelines influence development?

OWASP guidelines help shape secure coding practices, architecture reviews, threat modeling, code reviews, and security testing processes.

126. SQL Injection

Security

SQL Injection occurs when malicious SQL statements are inserted into application inputs and executed by the database engine. Attackers can use SQL Injection to read, modify, delete data, or bypass authentication mechanisms.

Potential Impact

  • Read Sensitive Data
  • Modify Existing Data
  • Delete Records
  • Bypass Authentication

Vulnerable Example

Unsafe SQL Construction
var sql =
 $"SELECT * FROM Users
   WHERE Name='{name}'";

If a malicious user enters the following input:

Malicious Input
' OR 1=1 --

The generated SQL becomes:

Injected SQL
SELECT * FROM Users
WHERE Name='' OR 1=1

Since the condition always evaluates to true, all records are returned.

Secure Example

Entity Framework LINQ Query
var user =
 await _context.Users
    .FirstOrDefaultAsync(
      x => x.Name == name);

Entity Framework automatically parameterizes LINQ queries, helping prevent SQL Injection attacks.

Follow-up Questions

Q: How do you prevent SQL Injection?

  • Parameterized Queries
  • Entity Framework
  • Input Validation

Q: Does EF Core prevent SQL Injection?

Generally yes, when using LINQ queries because EF Core automatically parameterizes query values.

Senior-Level Follow-up

Q: Can raw SQL still be vulnerable?

Yes. Unsafe string concatenation within raw SQL statements can still introduce SQL Injection vulnerabilities.

127. Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)

Security

Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) occurs when malicious JavaScript code is injected into a web page and executed in another user's browser.

Possible Consequences

  • Steal Cookies
  • Hijack Sessions
  • Redirect Users
  • Execute Malicious Scripts

Vulnerable Example

A user submits the following content:

Malicious Input
<script>
alert('Hacked');
</script>

If rendered directly into the page:

Unsafe Rendering
<div>
<script>
alert('Hacked');
</script>
</div>

The browser executes the injected JavaScript.

Prevention Techniques

  • Encode Output
  • Sanitize Input
  • Use Content Security Policy (CSP)

Follow-up Questions

Q: Is XSS server-side or client-side?

The attack executes within the user's browser, making it primarily a client-side security issue.

Q: Can APIs suffer from XSS?

Indirectly. APIs may return unsanitized content that becomes dangerous when rendered by a frontend application.

Senior-Level Follow-up

Q: How does React help reduce XSS?

React automatically escapes rendered values by default, reducing the risk of accidental script execution.

128. Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)

Security

Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) is an attack that tricks an authenticated user into unknowingly sending a request to a trusted application. Since browsers automatically include authentication cookies with requests, the server may treat the malicious request as legitimate.

How CSRF Works

  • User logs into a trusted application.
  • The browser stores authentication cookies.
  • The user visits a malicious website.
  • The malicious site triggers a request to the trusted application.
  • The browser automatically sends cookies with the request.

Real Project Example

Assume a user is logged into an online banking application.

Trusted Application
Bank Website

An attacker embeds the following content on a malicious website:

Malicious Request
<img src=
"https://bank.com/transfer?
amount=10000">

Because the browser automatically sends authentication cookies, the transfer request may be processed as if it originated from the user.

Prevention Techniques

  • Anti-Forgery Tokens
  • SameSite Cookies
  • CSRF Validation

Follow-up Questions

Q: Does JWT eliminate CSRF?

When JWT tokens are stored and transmitted using Authorization headers instead of cookies, CSRF risk is significantly reduced.

Q: Which applications are most vulnerable?

Applications that rely on cookie-based authentication are generally more vulnerable to CSRF attacks.

Senior-Level Follow-up

Q: Why are anti-forgery tokens effective?

Anti-forgery tokens work because attackers cannot predict or generate valid tokens required by the server.

129. CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing)

Security

CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) is a browser security mechanism that controls whether one domain can access resources from another domain. Without proper CORS configuration, browsers block cross-origin requests.

Key Concepts

  • Origin = Protocol + Domain + Port
  • Browsers enforce CORS restrictions
  • Servers define allowed origins
  • Helps control cross-origin access

Real Project Example

A frontend application and API are hosted on different domains.

Frontend
https://app.company.com
Backend API
https://api.company.com

The API must explicitly allow requests from the frontend origin.

ASP.NET Core Configuration

Add CORS Policy
builder.Services.AddCors(options =>
{
    options.AddPolicy("MyPolicy",
        policy =>
        {
            policy.AllowAnyOrigin()
                  .AllowAnyMethod()
                  .AllowAnyHeader();
        });
});

Follow-up Questions

Q: Why is CORS needed?

CORS provides controlled access to resources across different origins while maintaining browser security restrictions.

Q: Does CORS protect APIs?

Not directly. CORS primarily protects browsers and users by controlling which websites can access API responses.

Senior-Level Follow-up

Q: Why avoid AllowAnyOrigin in production?

Allowing every origin grants access to all domains, which may expose sensitive APIs to unintended clients.

130. HTTPS & TLS

Security

HTTPS is HTTP running over TLS (Transport Layer Security). It encrypts communication between clients and servers, preventing interception, tampering, and unauthorized access to data.

Benefits of HTTPS

  • Encryption
  • Data Integrity
  • Server Authentication
  • Protection Against Network Attacks

Real Project Example

HTTP
Data Sent In Plain Text
HTTPS
Encrypted Communication

HTTPS ensures that sensitive information such as credentials, payment details, and personal data remain encrypted while in transit.

ASP.NET Core Example

HTTPS Redirection
app.UseHttpsRedirection();

Follow-up Questions

Q: Why use HTTPS?

  • Encryption
  • Integrity
  • Authentication

Q: What is TLS?

TLS (Transport Layer Security) is the protocol responsible for securing and encrypting communications over HTTPS.

Senior-Level Follow-up

Q: What risks exist without HTTPS?

  • Data Theft
  • Session Hijacking
  • Man-in-the-Middle Attacks

131. Secrets Management

Security

Secrets such as API keys, passwords, certificates, and connection strings should never be hardcoded in source code or committed to source control. Proper secrets management is essential for protecting sensitive information and reducing security risks in production environments.

Examples of Secrets

  • Database Connection Strings
  • API Keys
  • JWT Signing Keys
  • Passwords
  • Certificates

Bad Example

Hardcoding secrets directly in source code exposes sensitive information to anyone with repository access.

Hardcoded Secret
string password =
"Admin123";

Better Approaches

  • Environment Variables
  • .NET Secret Manager
  • Azure Key Vault
  • AWS Secrets Manager
  • HashiCorp Vault

Follow-up Questions

Q: Why avoid storing secrets in Git?

Anyone with repository access can potentially view and misuse exposed credentials and sensitive information.

Q: Where should production secrets be stored?

Production secrets should be stored in dedicated secret-management systems that provide encryption, auditing, and access control.

Senior-Level Follow-up

Q: What is Azure Key Vault used for?

Azure Key Vault provides secure storage and controlled access to secrets, cryptographic keys, and certificates.

132. Performance Optimization

Performance

Performance optimization focuses on improving application speed, scalability, responsiveness, and resource utilization. The objective is to serve more requests efficiently while consuming fewer system resources.

Common Optimization Techniques

  • Caching
  • Async Programming
  • Database Optimization
  • Pagination
  • Query Optimization

Real Project Example

Fetching large datasets without pagination can significantly impact performance and memory consumption.

Bad Example
var users =
 await _context.Users.ToListAsync();

The above query may attempt to load millions of records into memory.

Optimized Example
var users =
 await _context.Users
      .Skip(0)
      .Take(100)
      .ToListAsync();

Pagination reduces memory usage and improves response times.

Performance Checklist

  • Use Pagination
  • Implement Caching
  • Optimize SQL Queries
  • Use Async/Await
  • Reduce Network Calls

Follow-up Questions

Q: What is the most common performance issue?

Inefficient database queries are among the most common causes of performance bottlenecks.

Q: Why use caching?

Caching reduces expensive computations and database calls, improving overall application performance.

Senior-Level Follow-up

Q: What do you check first during performance issues?

  • Database Queries
  • External API Calls
  • Memory Consumption
  • CPU Utilization

133. Memory Leaks

Diagnostics

A memory leak occurs when memory that is no longer needed cannot be reclaimed by the Garbage Collector because references to objects still exist.

Over time, leaked memory accumulates, causing increased memory usage, reduced performance, and potential application crashes.

Common Causes

  • Static Collections
  • Unreleased Event Subscriptions
  • Cached Objects Never Removed
  • Long-Lived References
  • Improper Resource Disposal

Real Project Example

Potential Memory Leak
public static List<User>
    CachedUsers = new();

Because the collection is static, objects may remain referenced for the lifetime of the application and never become eligible for garbage collection.

Symptoms of Memory Leaks

  • Increasing Memory Usage
  • Frequent Garbage Collection
  • Application Slowdowns
  • OutOfMemory Exceptions

Follow-up Questions

Q: Can .NET applications have memory leaks?

Yes. Garbage Collection reduces memory management complexity, but memory leaks can still occur when references remain active.

Q: What is a common source of memory leaks?

Forgotten event subscriptions are one of the most common causes of memory leaks in .NET applications.

Senior-Level Follow-up

Q: How do you detect memory leaks?

Memory profiling tools, heap analysis, diagnostics tracing, and monitoring solutions help identify leaked objects and long-lived references.

134. Profiling & Diagnostics

Performance & Monitoring

Profiling and diagnostics are techniques used to identify performance bottlenecks, memory leaks, excessive CPU usage, slow database queries, and application failures. These tools provide visibility into how an application behaves in development, testing, and production environments.

Why Profiling Matters

  • Identify Performance Bottlenecks
  • Detect Memory Leaks
  • Analyze CPU Usage
  • Investigate Slow Database Queries
  • Troubleshoot Production Issues

Common Diagnostic Tools

Tool Purpose
Visual Studio Diagnostic Tools Performance and Memory Analysis
dotnet-counters Runtime Performance Monitoring
dotnet-trace Collect Runtime Traces
Application Insights Production Monitoring and Telemetry
PerfView Advanced Performance Investigation

Real Project Example

A production API suddenly begins responding very slowly.

Issue Observed
API Response Time = 10 Seconds

After investigating using a profiler:

Investigation Flow
Profiler
   ↓
Slow SQL Query Found
   ↓
Database Index Added
   ↓
Response Time = 500ms

Profiling helped identify the real bottleneck instead of relying on assumptions.

Follow-up Questions

Q: Why use profiling tools?

Profiling tools help identify actual performance bottlenecks, allowing developers to make data-driven optimization decisions.

Q: What metrics are commonly monitored?

  • CPU Usage
  • Memory Consumption
  • Response Time
  • Request Throughput
  • Database Query Duration
  • Error Rates

Senior-Level Follow-up

Q: Why is monitoring important in production?

Many production issues cannot be reproduced locally. Continuous monitoring provides visibility into application health, performance trends, and unexpected failures.

135. System Design for .NET Interviews

Architecture

System Design focuses on building scalable, reliable, maintainable, secure, and high-performing applications. During interviews, candidates are evaluated on how they approach architecture decisions rather than their knowledge of specific syntax.

Areas Considered During System Design

  • Functional Requirements
  • Non-Functional Requirements
  • Database Design
  • Caching Strategy
  • Authentication & Authorization
  • Scalability
  • Monitoring & Logging
  • Deployment Strategy

Real Project Example

Design a high-traffic e-commerce platform capable of handling thousands of concurrent users.

High-Level Architecture
Client
  ↓
API Gateway
  ↓
Load Balancer
  ↓
ASP.NET Core APIs
  ↓
Redis Cache
  ↓
SQL Server

RabbitMQ

Background Workers

Architecture Components

Component Purpose
API Gateway Centralized Routing and Security
Load Balancer Distribute Incoming Traffic
ASP.NET Core APIs Business Logic Processing
Redis Cache Reduce Database Load
SQL Server Persistent Data Storage
RabbitMQ Asynchronous Processing
Background Workers Handle Long-Running Tasks

Follow-up Questions

Q: How do you handle high traffic?

  • Horizontal Scaling
  • Load Balancing
  • Caching
  • Database Optimization
  • Asynchronous Processing

Q: How do you improve reliability?

  • Health Checks
  • Retry Policies
  • Circuit Breakers
  • Monitoring & Alerts
  • Failover Strategies

Senior-Level Follow-up

Q: What separates a senior developer from a mid-level developer in system design?

A senior developer evaluates the entire system lifecycle and considers architectural trade-offs beyond implementation details.

  • Scalability
  • Fault Tolerance
  • Security
  • Maintainability
  • Observability
  • Operational Support
  • Cost Optimization

Interview Tip

During .NET System Design interviews, avoid jumping directly into implementation. First discuss requirements, traffic expectations, scalability needs, database choices, caching strategy, security requirements, monitoring, and deployment considerations before proposing the final architecture.

topics.title: Follow-up Questions
topics.html:
1. Why is String Immutable?

C# Fundamentals

String is immutable because once a string object is created, its value cannot be changed. Whenever a modification occurs, .NET creates a new string object instead of modifying the existing one.

Benefits of String Immutability

  • Thread Safety
  • Security
  • Hashing Performance
  • String Interning

Follow-up Question

Q: Then why doesn't this modify the string?

Example
string name = "John";

name += " Smith";

A new string object is created rather than modifying the existing one.

Internal Behavior
"John"
   ↓
"John Smith"

The original string remains unchanged.

Q: When should StringBuilder be used?

Use StringBuilder when performing multiple string modifications, especially inside loops.

2. Why is StringBuilder Faster?

C# Fundamentals

StringBuilder is mutable. Instead of creating new string objects for every modification, it updates an internal character buffer.

Advantages of StringBuilder

  • Fewer Memory Allocations
  • Reduced Garbage Collection
  • Better Performance for Repeated Updates
  • Efficient String Manipulation

Follow-up Question

Q: Is StringBuilder always faster?

No. For small string operations, normal string concatenation is usually sufficient. StringBuilder becomes beneficial when many modifications occur.

Small String Operation
string fullName = first + last;

3. Why is DbContext Scoped?

Entity Framework Core

DbContext is designed to represent a single unit of work per request. ASP.NET Core registers DbContext as Scoped by default because each HTTP request should receive its own DbContext instance.

Why Scoped?

  • One Unit of Work Per Request
  • Proper Change Tracking
  • Improved Data Consistency
  • Thread-Safe Request Processing

Follow-up Questions

Q: Why not Singleton?

  • DbContext is not thread-safe
  • Can cause Data Corruption
  • May create Concurrency Issues
  • Can result in Unexpected Behavior

Q: Why not Transient?

Multiple repositories may receive different DbContext instances during the same request, causing tracking and consistency issues.

4. Why is Repository Pattern Sometimes Avoided?

Design Patterns

Repository Pattern was originally designed to abstract data access. However, Entity Framework Core already provides implementations of Repository and Unit of Work patterns through DbContext.

EF Core Already Provides

  • Repository Pattern
  • Unit of Work Pattern
  • Change Tracking
  • Transaction Management

Follow-up Questions

Q: Is Repository Pattern always needed with EF Core?

No. Many modern applications use DbContext directly to avoid unnecessary abstraction layers.

Q: When is Repository useful?

  • Multiple Data Sources Exist
  • Complex Business Rules Exist
  • Testing Requires Abstraction

5. Why Use async/await?

Asynchronous Programming

async/await improves application scalability by preventing threads from being blocked while waiting for I/O operations such as database calls, API requests, or file operations.

Benefits of async/await

  • Improved Scalability
  • Better Resource Utilization
  • Responsive Applications
  • Efficient Thread Usage

Follow-up Questions

Q: Does async make code faster?

No. async improves scalability and responsiveness, not raw execution speed.

Q: Example?

Async Database Call
await _context.Users.ToListAsync();

While the database operation is running, the thread becomes available to process other requests.

6. What Happens Internally When await Is Encountered?

Asynchronous Programming

When the await keyword is encountered, the method does not block the current thread. Instead, the method is paused, the asynchronous operation continues, and execution resumes when the operation completes.

Internal Flow of await

  • Method execution pauses
  • Current thread is released
  • Asynchronous operation continues
  • Method resumes when operation completes
Execution Flow
Method Starts
      ↓
await
      ↓
Thread Released
      ↓
Operation Completes
      ↓
Method Resumes

Follow-up Question

Q: Does await create a new thread?

No. This is a common misconception. The await keyword itself does not create a new thread. It simply allows the current thread to be used elsewhere while waiting for the operation to finish.

7. Task vs Thread

Asynchronous Programming

A Thread is an operating system execution unit, while a Task is a higher-level abstraction used to represent asynchronous work.

Task Thread
Represents Work Represents Execution Unit
Lightweight More Expensive
Uses Thread Pool OS Managed
Preferred in Modern .NET Used Less Frequently

Follow-up Questions

Q: Does every Task create a Thread?

No. Most tasks use the .NET Thread Pool and do not create dedicated threads.

Q: Which should be preferred?

Task should generally be preferred because it provides a simpler, more scalable programming model.

8. Why Is Any() Better Than Count()?

LINQ

Any() is typically more efficient when checking whether records exist. It stops processing as soon as the first matching record is found, while Count() evaluates all matching records.

Performance Difference

  • Any() Stops Early
  • Count() Processes All Records
  • Less Database Work
  • Faster Existence Checks

Generated SQL

Any()
EXISTS(...)
Count()
COUNT(*)

EXISTS is generally more efficient because the database can stop searching after finding the first match.

9. FirstOrDefault vs SingleOrDefault

LINQ

Both methods return a single entity or null, but they differ in how they handle multiple matching records.

Method Behavior
FirstOrDefault() Returns First Match
SingleOrDefault() Requires Exactly One Match

Follow-up Questions

Q: Which should be used for Email?

SingleOrDefault() should be used because email addresses are typically unique.

Q: What if duplicates exist?

SingleOrDefault() throws an exception if more than one record matches the condition.

10. Why Dependency Injection?

Design Principles

Dependency Injection (DI) promotes loose coupling by allowing classes to depend on abstractions rather than concrete implementations. This improves maintainability, flexibility, and testability.

Benefits of Dependency Injection

  • Loose Coupling
  • Improved Testability
  • Better Maintainability
  • Easier Dependency Management

What Problem Does DI Solve?

Without Dependency Injection
new SqlRepository();

The class becomes tightly coupled to a specific implementation.

With Dependency Injection
IUserRepository

The implementation can be swapped without modifying the consuming class.

Interview Summary

Dependency Injection is one of the core design principles in ASP.NET Core and is essential for building scalable, maintainable, and testable applications.

11. Why Constructor Injection?

Dependency Injection

Constructor Injection is the most commonly recommended form of Dependency Injection because it makes dependencies explicit, mandatory, and available when an object is created.

Benefits of Constructor Injection

  • Dependencies Are Explicit
  • Object Is Always Valid
  • Improves Testability
  • Supports Immutable Dependencies

Example

Constructor Injection
public class UserService
{
    private readonly IUserRepository _repository;

    public UserService(IUserRepository repository)
    {
        _repository = repository;
    }
}

Follow-up Question

Q: Why not Property Injection?

Property Injection can allow objects to be created in an invalid state because required dependencies may never be assigned.

Potential Problems

  • Missing Dependencies
  • Runtime Errors
  • Harder Testing
  • Less Predictable Object State

12. Why Middleware Instead Of Writing Logic In Controllers?

ASP.NET Core

Middleware is designed to handle cross-cutting concerns that apply to multiple requests. Instead of duplicating logic in controllers, middleware allows centralized request processing.

Common Middleware Scenarios

  • Logging
  • Authentication
  • Authorization
  • Exception Handling
  • Request Validation
  • CORS Processing

Request Pipeline

ASP.NET Core Request Flow
Request
   ↓
Middleware
   ↓
Controller
   ↓
Response

Follow-up Question

Q: What is the main benefit?

Middleware eliminates duplicated code and ensures consistent behavior across the entire application.

13. Why Authentication Before Authorization?

Security

Authentication must occur before Authorization because authorization requires a verified user identity. The system must first determine who the user is before deciding what the user can access.

Processing Order

  • Authenticate User
  • Create User Identity
  • Evaluate Permissions
  • Authorize Access

Request Flow

Correct Pipeline Order
Request
   ↓
Authentication
   ↓
Authorization
   ↓
Controller

Follow-up Question

Q: What happens if the order is reversed?

Authorization will fail because no authenticated user identity exists yet for permission evaluation.

14. Why JWT Instead Of Session?

Authentication

JWT (JSON Web Token) is a stateless authentication mechanism. Unlike traditional sessions, JWT does not require server-side session storage, making it ideal for distributed systems.

JWT Session
Stateless Stateful
No Server Storage Requires Server Storage
Scales Easily More Difficult to Scale
Microservice Friendly Better for Traditional Apps

Follow-up Question

Q: Why is JWT useful for Microservices?

Every service can independently validate the token without needing shared session storage.

15. Why Refresh Tokens?

Authentication

Refresh Tokens allow applications to use short-lived access tokens while maintaining a seamless user experience. When an access token expires, a refresh token can be used to obtain a new one without requiring the user to log in again.

Benefits of Refresh Tokens

  • Improved Security
  • Short-Lived Access Tokens
  • Better User Experience
  • Reduced Risk of Token Theft

Authentication Flow

Token Lifecycle
Login
   ↓
Access Token Issued
   ↓
Access Token Expires
   ↓
Refresh Token Used
   ↓
New Access Token Issued

Follow-up Question

Q: Why not use long-lived JWTs?

Long-lived JWTs increase security risks because a stolen token remains valid for a longer period of time.

16. Why Use Redis?

Caching

Redis is an in-memory data store commonly used for distributed caching, session storage, pub/sub messaging, and high-performance data access. It helps reduce database load and improve application response times.

Benefits of Redis

  • Extremely Fast Data Access
  • Distributed Caching
  • Reduced Database Load
  • Supports Multiple Servers
  • Improved Scalability

Architecture Example

Distributed Cache Flow
Application
      ↓
Redis Cache
      ↓
Database

Follow-up Question

Q: Why not Memory Cache?

Memory Cache exists only within a single application instance. Redis can be shared across multiple servers, making it suitable for distributed environments.

17. Why Use RabbitMQ?

Messaging

RabbitMQ is a message broker that enables asynchronous communication between applications and services. It helps decouple systems and improves reliability by allowing messages to be processed independently.

Benefits of RabbitMQ

  • Asynchronous Processing
  • Loose Coupling
  • Improved Reliability
  • Message Persistence
  • Scalable Architecture

Messaging Flow

RabbitMQ Workflow
Producer
   ↓
RabbitMQ
   ↓
Consumer

Follow-up Question

Q: Why not direct API calls?

Direct API calls create tight coupling between services. Queues improve fault tolerance and allow systems to process messages independently.

18. Why Use CQRS?

Architecture

CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation) separates read operations from write operations. This allows each side to be optimized independently and simplifies complex business logic.

CQRS Principles

  • Commands Modify Data
  • Queries Read Data
  • Separate Responsibilities
  • Independent Optimization

CQRS Structure

CQRS Flow
Commands
    ↓
Write Database

Queries
    ↓
Read Database

Follow-up Question

Q: Should every application use CQRS?

No. CQRS introduces additional complexity and should only be used when the benefits outweigh the architectural costs.

19. Why Use MediatR?

Architecture

MediatR is a library that implements the Mediator pattern. It helps reduce coupling between controllers and business logic by routing requests through handlers.

Benefits of MediatR

  • Reduced Coupling
  • Cleaner Controllers
  • Better Separation of Concerns
  • Supports CQRS Implementations

Traditional Approach

Without MediatR
Controller
    ↓
Service
    ↓
Repository

MediatR Approach

With MediatR
Controller
    ↓
Mediator
    ↓
Handler

Follow-up Question

Q: Is MediatR mandatory for CQRS?

No. CQRS is an architectural pattern, while MediatR is simply a tool that can help implement it.

20. Why Use Clean Architecture?

Architecture

Clean Architecture organizes an application into layers and ensures that business rules remain independent of frameworks, databases, UI technologies, and external systems.

Core Principles

  • Separation of Concerns
  • Dependency Inversion
  • Independent Business Logic
  • Framework Independence
  • Improved Testability

Layered Structure

Clean Architecture Layers
Presentation
      ↓
Application
      ↓
Domain
      ↓
Infrastructure

Follow-up Question

Q: What is the biggest advantage?

Technology changes such as replacing databases, frameworks, or external services do not impact the core business rules.

Interview Tip

Senior developers often describe Clean Architecture as a way to protect business logic from infrastructure concerns rather than simply organizing projects into folders.

21. Why Is EF Core Tracking Expensive?

Entity Framework Core

EF Core tracks entities by storing information about their state and property values. This allows EF Core to detect changes and generate appropriate SQL statements when SaveChanges() is called.

While tracking is useful for updates, it consumes additional memory and CPU resources, especially when loading large datasets.

Why Tracking Has Overhead

  • Stores Entity State
  • Monitors Property Changes
  • Consumes Additional Memory
  • Requires Extra CPU Processing

Performance Optimization

For read-only queries, tracking can be disabled to improve performance.

Read-Only Query
_context.Users
        .AsNoTracking()
        .ToListAsync();

Q: How can performance be improved?

Use AsNoTracking() for read-only operations to reduce memory usage and tracking overhead.

22. Why Use Pagination?

Performance Optimization

Pagination prevents large datasets from being loaded into memory at once. It improves application performance, reduces memory consumption, and provides a better user experience.

Benefits of Pagination

  • Reduced Memory Usage
  • Faster Response Times
  • Improved Scalability
  • Better User Experience

Example

Bad Practice
Users.ToList()

This loads all records into memory.

Recommended Approach
Users.Skip(0)
     .Take(50)

Only the required records are retrieved from the database.

Interview Tip

Whenever an API returns large collections, discuss pagination, filtering, and sorting as part of the solution.

23. Why Use Health Checks?

Monitoring

Health Checks allow monitoring systems to determine whether an application and its dependencies are functioning correctly.

What Can Be Checked?

  • Database Connectivity
  • External APIs
  • Message Queues
  • Disk Availability
  • Application Status

Health Check Flow

Monitoring Process
Monitoring Tool
        ↓
/health Endpoint
        ↓
Healthy / Unhealthy

Follow-up Question

Q: Who consumes health endpoints?

  • Kubernetes
  • Load Balancers
  • Monitoring Tools
  • Cloud Platforms

24. Why Use Docker?

DevOps

Docker packages applications together with their dependencies, configuration, and runtime environment into lightweight containers.

This ensures that applications run consistently across development, testing, staging, and production environments.

Benefits of Docker

  • Environment Consistency
  • Simplified Deployment
  • Isolation of Applications
  • Scalability Support
  • Faster Setup

Container Architecture

Docker Environment
Application
      +
Dependencies
      +
Runtime
      ↓
Docker Container

Follow-up Question

Q: What is the main advantage of Docker?

Docker eliminates the classic: 

Works on my machine

problem by ensuring the same environment everywhere.

25. Why Use Kubernetes?

DevOps

Kubernetes is a container orchestration platform that automates deployment, scaling, load balancing, and recovery of containerized applications.

Kubernetes Responsibilities

  • Container Deployment
  • Auto Scaling
  • Load Balancing
  • Self-Healing
  • Rolling Updates

High-Level Architecture

Kubernetes Workflow
User Traffic
      ↓
Load Balancer
      ↓
Pods
      ↓
Containers

Follow-up Question

Q: What happens if a container crashes?

Kubernetes automatically detects the failure and recreates the container to maintain the desired application state.

Interview Tip

When discussing Kubernetes in interviews, emphasize auto-scaling, self-healing, rolling deployments, and high availability rather than simply calling it a container manager.

26. Why Use SignalR?

Real-Time Communication

SignalR is an ASP.NET Core library that enables real-time communication between servers and connected clients. It allows the server to push updates instantly without requiring clients to continuously poll for data.

Benefits of SignalR

  • Real-Time Updates
  • Server Push Communication
  • Reduced Polling
  • Improved User Experience
  • Supports Multiple Transport Mechanisms

Common Use Cases

  • Chat Applications
  • Notifications
  • Live Dashboards
  • Stock Market Updates
  • Online Gaming

Real-Time Flow

SignalR Communication
Server
   ↓
SignalR Hub
   ↓
Connected Clients

Follow-up Question

Q: Why not use API polling?

Polling generates unnecessary requests even when data has not changed. SignalR pushes updates only when new information becomes available.

27. Why Use gRPC?

Microservices

gRPC is a high-performance communication framework built on HTTP/2. It is commonly used for service-to-service communication in distributed systems.

Benefits of gRPC

  • High Performance
  • Smaller Payloads
  • Strongly Typed Contracts
  • Bi-Directional Streaming
  • Efficient Service Communication

REST vs gRPC

REST gRPC
JSON Payloads Protocol Buffers
Larger Messages Smaller Messages
Text Based Binary Format
Typically Slower Typically Faster

Follow-up Question

Q: Why is gRPC faster than REST?

Protocol Buffers are compact binary messages that require less bandwidth and faster serialization than JSON.

28. Why Use Caching?

Performance Optimization

Caching stores frequently accessed data in a faster storage layer, reducing expensive database queries and external API calls.

Benefits of Caching

  • Reduced Database Load
  • Faster Response Times
  • Improved Scalability
  • Lower Infrastructure Costs
  • Better User Experience

Cache Flow

Request Processing
Request
   ↓
Cache Hit?
   ↓
Yes → Return Cached Data

No
 ↓
Database
 ↓
Store In Cache
 ↓
Return Data

Follow-up Question

Q: What should be cached?

  • Frequently Read Data
  • Rarely Changing Data
  • Reference Data
  • Configuration Data

29. Why Is Singleton Dangerous?

Dependency Injection

Singleton services are created only once and shared across the entire application lifetime. While useful in some scenarios, they can introduce risks when they manage mutable shared state.

Potential Risks

  • Thread Safety Issues
  • Shared Mutable State
  • Memory Retention Problems
  • Harder Debugging
  • Unexpected Side Effects

Service Lifetime Comparison

Lifetime Created
Transient Every Request
Scoped Once Per HTTP Request
Singleton Once Per Application

Follow-up Question

Q: What is the main risk?

Thread safety issues can occur when multiple requests access and modify shared state simultaneously.

30. Why Use ILogger Instead Of Console.WriteLine?

Logging

ILogger is the recommended logging abstraction in ASP.NET Core. It provides structured logging, filtering, multiple log providers, and integration with monitoring platforms.

ILogger Features

  • Log Levels
  • Structured Logging
  • Multiple Providers
  • Centralized Logging
  • Production Monitoring Support

Log Levels

Level Purpose
Trace Detailed Diagnostics
Debug Development Information
Information Application Events
Warning Potential Issues
Error Failures
Critical Application-Critical Failures

Example

ILogger Usage
_logger.LogInformation(
    "User {UserId} logged in",
    userId);

Follow-up Question

Q: What should be used in production?

Use ILogger together with logging providers such as Serilog, Application Insights, Seq, Elasticsearch, or cloud monitoring platforms.

Interview Tip

Avoid using Console.WriteLine in production applications because it lacks structured logging, filtering, persistence, and monitoring capabilities.

topics.title: Scenario Based .NET Interview Questions
topics.html:
1. API Suddenly Becomes Slow in Production

Production Troubleshooting

Interview Question

Your API response time increased from 200ms to 10 seconds in production. How would you investigate?

Interview Answer

I would follow a structured troubleshooting approach rather than making assumptions. First, I would identify where the bottleneck exists and then use monitoring, logging, and profiling tools to isolate the root cause.

Areas To Investigate

  • Database
  • External APIs
  • Application Code
  • Infrastructure
  • Network

I would review logs, monitoring dashboards, SQL query performance, CPU usage, memory consumption, and any recent deployments.

Investigation Flow

Troubleshooting Process
Application Insights
        ↓
Slow Endpoint
        ↓
SQL Query Analysis
        ↓
Execution Plan
        ↓
Root Cause

Follow-up Questions

Q: What do you check first?

Response time metrics and recent deployments.

Q: Most common cause?

Slow database queries.

2. Memory Usage Keeps Increasing

Memory Management

Interview Question

Application memory keeps increasing every day until restart. What would you do?

Interview Answer

This typically indicates a memory leak or excessive object retention. I would collect diagnostic data and identify which objects are preventing memory from being reclaimed.

Investigation Steps

  • Capture Memory Dumps
  • Use Profiling Tools
  • Analyze Object References
  • Check Static Collections
  • Review Event Subscriptions

Common Causes

Memory Leak Sources
Static Lists

Large Cache

Event Handlers

Singleton Misuse

Follow-up Question

Q: Can .NET have memory leaks?

Yes. Garbage Collection cannot clean objects that are still referenced.

3. JWT Token Is Valid But API Returns 401

Authentication

Interview Question

User sends a JWT token but API returns 401 Unauthorized.

Interview Answer

I would validate all JWT configuration settings and verify that the token is being sent correctly.

Verification Checklist

  • Token Expiration
  • Signing Key
  • Issuer
  • Audience
  • Authorization Header Format

Common Checks

Correct Header
Authorization: Bearer Token
Incorrect Header
Authorization: Token

Follow-up Question

Q: Most common issue?

Expired token or incorrect JWT configuration.

4. Database Receiving Too Many Queries

Entity Framework Core

Interview Question

Database CPU is high because the application is generating excessive queries.

Interview Answer

I would investigate inefficient query patterns and identify whether Entity Framework is generating unnecessary database calls.

Areas To Investigate

  • N+1 Queries
  • Missing Includes
  • Missing Caching
  • Inefficient LINQ Queries

Bad Example

N+1 Query Problem
foreach(var order in orders)
{
    var customer =
        order.Customer;
}

This can generate multiple database queries.

Better Approach

Eager Loading
_context.Orders
        .Include(x => x.Customer);

Q: Common EF Core issue?

The N+1 Query Problem.

5. Application Works Locally But Fails In Docker

Docker Troubleshooting

Interview Question

API works locally but fails after Docker deployment.

Interview Answer

I would compare the container environment with the local environment and review configuration differences.

Verification Checklist

  • Environment Variables
  • Ports
  • Connection Strings
  • File Paths
  • Container Logs

Common Docker Issue

localhost Inside Container
localhost
      ↓
Container Itself

Inside a container, localhost refers to the container itself, not the host machine.

Q: First thing to check?

Container logs.

6. Need To Improve API Performance

Performance Optimization

Interview Question

How would you improve API performance?

Interview Answer

I would first identify bottlenecks through profiling and monitoring, then optimize the areas that have the highest impact on response times and resource consumption.

Optimization Areas

  • Database Optimization
  • Caching
  • Async Programming
  • Pagination
  • Query Optimization

Example Optimization

Read-Only Query
.AsNoTracking()

Disabling tracking for read-only operations reduces memory usage and improves query performance.

Q: Biggest performance bottleneck?

Database operations are usually the most common bottleneck.

7. Users Report Random Application Crashes

Production Support

Interview Question

Production application occasionally crashes.

Interview Answer

I would gather diagnostic information before making conclusions. The goal is to identify patterns and determine whether the crashes are caused by application code, infrastructure, or external dependencies.

Data To Collect

  • Application Logs
  • Stack Traces
  • Crash Dumps
  • Exception Details

Investigation Flow

Crash Analysis
Crash
   ↓
Logs
   ↓
Stack Trace
   ↓
Root Cause
   ↓
Fix

Q: Should exceptions be swallowed?

No. Exceptions should always be logged and handled appropriately.

8. Design Notification System For 1 Million Users

System Design

Interview Question

How would you design a notification system for one million users?

Interview Answer

I would use an asynchronous architecture to prevent API requests from waiting for notification delivery operations.

Architecture Design

Notification Flow
API
 ↓
RabbitMQ
 ↓
Notification Worker
 ↓
Email/SMS Provider

Benefits

  • Scalability
  • Reliability
  • Retry Support
  • Loose Coupling

Q: Why not send emails directly?

Direct email sending makes requests slower and creates reliability issues when external providers are unavailable.

9. Database Query Takes 20 Seconds

Database Performance

Interview Question

How would you troubleshoot a database query that takes 20 seconds?

Interview Answer

I would analyze the execution plan and investigate indexing, query design, and data volume before attempting optimizations.

Investigation Checklist

  • Execution Plan
  • Indexes
  • Query Structure
  • Table Size
  • Statistics

Troubleshooting Flow

Database Analysis
Slow Query
     ↓
Execution Plan
     ↓
Missing Index
     ↓
Optimization
     ↓
Improved Performance

Q: Most common fix?

Adding proper indexes.

10. API Must Handle 10,000 Requests Per Minute

Scalability

Interview Question

How would you scale an API to handle 10,000 requests per minute?

Interview Answer

I would scale horizontally and reduce unnecessary load on application and database resources.

Scaling Components

  • Load Balancer
  • Multiple API Instances
  • Redis Cache
  • Database Optimization

Scalable Architecture

Horizontal Scaling
Load Balancer
      ↓

API 1

API 2

API 3

Interview Tip

When discussing scalability, mention caching, load balancing, database optimization, and horizontal scaling together for a complete production-ready answer.

11. Need Audit Logging

Auditing & Compliance

Interview Question

Every data change must be tracked. How would you implement audit logging?

Interview Answer

I would implement centralized audit logging so that every important data modification can be tracked for security, compliance, and troubleshooting purposes.

Audit Information To Store

  • User Information
  • Timestamp
